etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English deserven, from Old French deservir, from Latin dēserviō, from dē- + serviō.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To be entitled to, as a result of past actions; to be worthy to have.

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Job 11:6:
quote.text: God exacteth of thee less than thine iniquity deserveth.

quote.citation: 1853, William Makepeace Thackeray, The English Humorists of the Eighteenth Century:
quote.text: John Gay deserved to be a favourite.
the grantees named in the questioned deed executed by their father richly deserved receiving the family home.

quote.citation: 2008, Michael Walzer, Spheres Of Justice: A Defense Of Pluralism And Equality, page 24:
quote.text: Perhaps they do, but they don't deserve that the rest of us contribute money or appropriate public funds for the purchase of pictures and the construction of buildings.

quote.citation: 1590, Edmund Spenser, “Book III, Canto VII”, in The Faerie Queene. […], London:  […]  [John Wolfe] for William Ponsonbie, →OCLC:
quote.text: That gentle Lady, whom I loue and serue, / After long suit and weary seruicis, / Did aske me, how I could her loue deserue, / And how she might be sure, that I would neuer swerue.

definitions.definition: (obsolete) To reward, to give in return for service.

quote.citation: 1485, Sir Thomas Malory, chapter XXX, in Le Morte Darthur, book VIII:
quote.text: Gramercy saide the kynge / & I lyue sir Lambegus I shal deserue hit / And thenne sir Lambegus armed hym / and rode after as fast as he myghte(please add an English translation of this quotation)

quote.citation: c. 1603–1604 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Tragedie of Othello, the Moore of Venice”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, (please specify the act number in uppercase Roman numerals, and the scene number in lowercase Roman numerals):
quote.text: Pray you, lead on. At every house I'll call; / I may command at most. Get weapons, ho! / And raise some special officers of night. / On, good Roderigo: I'll deserve your pains.

definitions.definition: (obsolete) To serve; to treat; to benefit.

quote.citation: c. 1619–22, Philip Massinger and John Fletcher, A Very Woman
quote.text: A man that hath / So well deserved me.
